title: Post-quantum standards are not migration
summary: A qualitative technology-readiness map showing how NIST post-quantum cryptography standards create a migration clock, while institution-level implementation evidence remains unresolved.
map_question: How do post-quantum cryptography standards become operational migration work, and where does FTFN still lack implementation evidence?
interpretation_boundary: This map shows that standards progress can create a security migration clock. It does not prove that any institution, vendor, sector, or local system has completed post-quantum migration.

nodes.label: Quantum
nodes.note: The topic frame connects quantum risk, standards, infrastructure obligations, and human-system migration choices.

nodes.label: NIST Post-Quantum Cryptography Project
nodes.note: A Tier 1 standards source for PQC standards and migration context.

nodes.label: NIST PQC standards signal
nodes.note: An in-review security signal framing PQC as near-term migration work rather than distant theory.

nodes.label: Post-Quantum Cryptography
nodes.note: A source-backed technology profile for standards, algorithms, validation, and migration practices.

nodes.label: Standards adoption
nodes.note: Standards must be adopted through inventories, procurement rules, software updates, validation, and vendor support.

nodes.label: Cybersecurity migration
nodes.note: Migration risk is shaped by legacy systems, stored encrypted data, critical infrastructure exposure, staffing, and execution timelines.

nodes.label: Institution-level migration evidence
nodes.note: FTFN still needs procurement, inventory, vendor-readiness, and implementation evidence before stronger migration claims.

what_this_map_supports: FTFN can distinguish standards progress from operational migration progress.
FTFN can show how a standards source, a security signal, a technology profile, and an evidence gap fit together.
Post-quantum cryptography can be tracked as infrastructure migration work without numeric scoring.
what_this_map_does_not_prove: It does not prove that any institution has completed post-quantum migration.
It does not prove vendor readiness, procurement compliance, cryptographic inventory completeness, or critical-infrastructure execution.
It does not rank quantum risk or create a 42/59 score.
